mathematical_scope.weird: sigma(N)>2*N and no subset of the proper divisors sums to N
mathematical_scope.primitive_weird: weird and no proper divisor is weird
mathematical_scope.finite_template: k=12; every source prime p in (8191,16382); exactly q=8191+floor(8191^2/(p-8191)) per p
mathematical_scope.omitted_families: other q values, other k values, odd numbers and general primitive-weird enumeration
mathematical_scope.failure_scope: composite q means this prime-template certificate does not apply; template_N is not thereby classified as non-weird

published_criterion.authors: Gianluca Amato, Maximilian F. Hasler, Giuseppe Melfi, Maurizio Parton
published_criterion.title: Primitive weird numbers having more than three distinct prime factors
published_criterion.specialization: m=2^k, two primes, j=0; S<delta<p; p>S+1 follows from odd p and S

original_definitions.title: On Weird and Pseudoperfect Numbers
original_definitions.caution: historical nonstrict abundance convention; perfect numbers already have a proper-divisor subset summing to N

construction_observation.interpretation: one connected V8 observation, not a statistical benchmark

basis.premise: the listed integers are exactly all primes at most limit; not re-established here

construction.criterion: S < delta < p < q; p and q distinct odd primes; N=2^k*p*q
construction.published_specialization: Amato--Hasler--Melfi--Parton (2016), Theorem 3.1.1, m=2^k, two primes, j=0
construction.composite_scope: a composite q only fails this prime-template certificate; no classification of template_N as non-weird
